solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Ostentatious in a smock?

definitions.meaning: wearing clothes far too showy or formal for the occasion
a smock is a loose garment pulled over the rest, so the wearer is clothed in an over-garment

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful second reading: dressed in an over-garment.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone showily got up in excessive finery is said to be dressed beyond what is needed.

clue.text: Reluctant to lose a few lines

indicators.note: to lose says a letter is dropped from the word for reluctant

parts.note: averse means unwilling or reluctant

explanation.surface: Someone is unwilling to give up a handful of lines of text.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to lose a' takes the A off AVERSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A short stretch of poetry, a few lines long, is a stanza or passage of poetry.

clue.text: I arrive dishevelled from coastal area

indicators.note: dishevelled means messed up, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A traveller turns up rumpled after a trip from the seaside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dishevelled' rearranges the seven letters of I ARRIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Riviera is a famous stretch of Mediterranean coastline, a coastal region by name.

clue.text: Corresponding with daughter, say

definitions.meaning: a daughter is one example of a family member

explanation.definitionFit: Relative to means in proportion to; a daughter is an example of a kinsperson.

clue.text: Henry prepared to go above third son

indicators.note: in a down answer one piece placed above another comes before it

parts.note: set means ready or prepared
H is the abbreviation for henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A man named Henry is ready to outrank the youngest of three boys.
explanation.walkthrough: SETH was the third son of Adam and Eve in Genesis.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible Adam and Eve's third named son, after Cain and Abel, is Seth.

clue.text: What is the dentist doing? Exercising

definitions.meaning: a dentist bores into a tooth with a rotating tool
military drill means training exercises, so troops at practice are doing this

explanation.definitionFit: Boring a tooth is one sense; drilling soldiers is exercising them in formation.

clue.text: I name officer in most cases

parts.note: a general is a senior army officer

explanation.surface: A soldier gives the name of a high-ranking officer, as usually happens.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means generally or usually, true in the majority of cases.

clue.text: Nothing to write inside present for sale to highest bidder

parts.note: O, the round figure zero, stands for nothing
to pen something is to write it
taken as written
to present something is to offer it

explanation.surface: A gift with no message written in it is put up for auction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' only helps the surface (writing inside a card); the pieces simply follow one another.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods described this way will be sold to whoever makes an acceptable bid, ideally the highest.

clue.text: Approach time for preparation

definitions.meaning: the sprint an athlete or bowler makes before jumping or delivering
the period leading up to an event, as in the weeks before an election

explanation.definitionFit: A bowler's approach to the crease and the lead-in period before an event share this hyphenated term.

clue.text: Stop including one pound that's most common

indicators.note: including means the word for stop holds the other letters

parts.note: to prevent something is to stop it
A is the indefinite article, meaning one
L, from Latin libra, is the abbreviation for a pound

explanation.surface: Halting the inclusion of a single pound coin that is the usual one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'including' puts AL inside PREVENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something widespread and encountered most often is described as prevailing or widespread.

clue.text: Be at home after short break for painter

indicators.note: after says the be-at-home pieces follow the break

parts.note: HOL is holiday shortened, holiday being a break
taken as written
in means at home, as in 'staying in'

explanation.surface: Instruction to stay home once a brief vacation is over, signed by an artist.
explanation.walkthrough: Hans HOLBEIN was a German-Swiss Renaissance portrait painter at Henry VIII's court.
explanation.definitionFit: Hans Holbein the Younger is a celebrated Tudor-era portrait artist.

clue.text: It is likely to be found at the end of the column

definitions.text: It is likely to be found at the end of the column

parts.words: It is likely to be found at the end of the column
parts.note: reads like a footnote in a newspaper column, but means the base under a pillar

explanation.definitionFit: A pillar stands on a plinth or base at its foot, the bottom end of the column.

clue.text: Fine shot?

parts.note: a penalty is a fine or punishment
a kick at goal is a shot in football

explanation.surface: Someone admires a well-struck strike at goal.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: a shot awarded as a punishment. 'Fine' looks like praise but means a sanction.
explanation.definitionFit: In football a foul in the box is punished with a free strike at goal from the spot.

clue.text: Shakespearean, despite real trouble, set out

indicators.note: trouble means disturbance, so the letters of real are stirred up
out means wrong or disordered, so the letters of set are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Shakespeare actor set off in spite of genuine difficulties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' turns REAL into LAER and 'out' turns SET into TES.
explanation.definitionFit: Laertes, Ophelia's brother in Hamlet, is a Shakespearean character.

clue.text: Undignified leading character on the air performing

indicators.note: performing means acting up, so these letters put on a new show

explanation.surface: A star of a radio broadcast behaves without dignity while on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'performing' rearranges ON THE AIR.
explanation.definitionFit: A protagonist lacking heroic qualities such as dignity or nobility is the classic flawed lead.

clue.text: Part of sudden ovation is for the star

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some of a spontaneous round of applause is meant for the lead performer.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'is for the star' cannot stand in for the answer; 'is for the' are link words and 'star' alone is defined.
explanation.definitionFit: A nova is a star that suddenly flares up in brightness.

clue.text: My servant could have been member of parish council

indicators.note: could have been says the letters might be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: Someone muses that their domestic helper might once have sat on the local church committee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could have been' rearranges MY SERVANT.
explanation.definitionFit: A vestryman sits on the vestry, the body that runs a parish's affairs.

clue.text: Supporting part of machine

definitions.meaning: carrying or holding up a load
a ball or roller component that lets a shaft turn smoothly

explanation.definitionFit: Something bearing weight supports it; a machine bearing is a component reducing friction.

clue.text: Soothing oil said to come from castle

parts.note: balm is a fragrant soothing ointment or oil
oral means spoken or said aloud

explanation.surface: A calming ointment reportedly originates from a fortress.
explanation.walkthrough: BALMORAL is the British royal family's castle in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Balmoral is a royal residence in Aberdeenshire, a Scottish castle.

clue.text: Grit mixed with neon gas

indicators.note: mixed means stirred together, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Fine stones are combined with a noble gas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixed' rearranges GRIT and NEON together.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitrogen is the colourless gas making up most of the atmosphere.

clue.text: Symbol for the most part split

indicators.note: for the most part means most of the word for split is used, its last letter dropped

parts.note: cleft means split or divided

explanation.surface: A sign that is largely divided.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the most part' drops the final T of CLEFT.
explanation.definitionFit: A clef is a musical symbol on a stave fixing the pitch of the notes.

clue.text: 'Felix!'

parts.note: Felix is a classic name for a pet tabby, so shouting it is summoning one; also a derisive shout

explanation.definitionFit: A whistle or jeer of derision shares its name with a summons to a pet feline.

clue.text: Second person in Paris allowed back with plenty of time for private tuition

parts.note: tu is French for 'you', the second person singular

indicators.note: back says the word for allowed is turned round

parts.note: let means allowed
an age is a long time

explanation.surface: A French tutor permitted to return with ample time to give one-to-one lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns LET into TEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutelage is instruction given by a tutor, typically individual guidance.

clue.text: Spray hesitantly put on drink

parts.note: to spritz is to spray in a fine mist
er is the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: Someone haltingly mists a beverage.
explanation.walkthrough: A SPRITZER is white wine topped up with soda water.
explanation.definitionFit: A spritzer is a long drink of wine mixed with soda water.

clue.text: Pleaded but not initially encouraged

indicators.note: not initially means the first letter of the word for pleaded goes

parts.note: begged means pleaded

explanation.surface: Someone asked earnestly but was not cheered on at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not initially' removes the B of BEGGED.
explanation.definitionFit: To egg someone on is to urge or encourage them.

clue.text: Opening in modern surgery

definitions.meaning: the small hole a key goes into in a lock
the minimally invasive operating technique through tiny incisions

explanation.definitionFit: A lock's aperture for a key, and the minimally invasive surgical technique, share this name.

clue.text: Lamb, priest starting academy

parts.note: Eli is the priest who raised Samuel in the Bible

indicators.note: starting means the opening letter of academy

explanation.surface: A young sheep and a cleric begin at a school.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Lamb wrote his essays under the pen name ELIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Elia was the pseudonym of the essayist Charles Lamb.

clue.text: Travelling considerable distance to large working farm

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
on means operating or working
a grange is a farmhouse with its outbuildings

explanation.surface: A long trip to a big operational farmstead.
explanation.definitionFit: Missiles or flights covering great distances are described with this hyphenated adjective.

clue.text: Lady accountant, about 50, soldiers on

indicators.note: about says the accountant's letters go round the fifty

parts.note: CA is a chartered accountant
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
RA is the Royal Artillery, a body of soldiers

explanation.surface: A woman accountant of around fifty presses on with the troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts the Roman fifty inside the accountant's letters; 'on' simply joins the soldiers to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Clara is a woman's first name, so a lady may be called this.

clue.text: Usherette is a headliner

definitions.meaning: a woman who leads patrons to their seats in a cinema
the actress who takes the main female role in a production

explanation.definitionFit: A woman guiding cinemagoers is literally a lady leading; a star actress is billed as the female lead.
